directive.name: git
directive.description: Simple git workflow: everything on main, conventional commits as we go. No branching, no merging. Task artifacts are committed alongside code. This directive owns ALL git operations.

context.principle: All work happens on main. No feature branches.

All commits follow conventional commit format: type(#NNN): description. The scope is the task's numeric prefix only (e.g., #022 from id "022-add-dark-mode"). Valid types: feat, fix, docs, refactor, chore. Use "chore" for task scaffolding (create, scope, plan, save, done, rework, delete). Use "docs" only for actual product/engineering documentation. Use feat/fix/refactor/docs for implementation commits (derived from task label).
Task artifacts (.festinalente/tasks/, .festinalente/quick/) are committed to git.

process.rule: After writing the spec and updated task file, stage and commit: - git add .festinalente/tasks/{id}/spec.xml .festinalente/tasks/{id}/task.xml - git commit -m "chore(#{number}): scope - {title}"
After writing the plan and updated task file, stage and commit: - git add .festinalente/tasks/{id}/plan.xml .festinalente/tasks/{id}/task.xml - git commit -m "chore(#{number}): plan - {title}"
Do NOT commit during implementation. Code stays uncommitted until save or finalize.
Check for uncommitted changes: - Run: git status - Run: git diff --name-only If no changes found, warn the user and exit early (still update plan if needed).

Stage and commit all relevant files: - git add {changed code files} - git add .festinalente/tasks/{id}/ - git commit -m "chore(#{number}): save - {progress summary}" The summary should briefly describe what was completed.

During Phase 1: when a directive check fails and auto-fix is applied, commit the fix: - git add {files changed by the fix} - git commit -m "fix(#{number}): check-retry - {title}" Then restart all checks from the beginning.

After all three phases are complete (validation passed, docs written, status set to awaiting-completion), commit the implementation: 1. Check for uncommitted changes: git status && git diff --name-only Display files that will be committed. If none, warn user and ask whether to proceed. 2. Determine commit type from the task's label using the commit-type field in workflow.yaml: bug→fix, feature→feat, docs→docs, refactor→refactor. Default: feat. 3. Stage and commit code + task artifacts: - git add {implementation code files} - git add .festinalente/tasks/{id}/ - git commit -m "{commitType}(#{number}): {title}"

After G-FIN-COMMIT, if Phase 2 updated documentation, commit docs separately: - git add .festinalente/product/ .festinalente/engineering/ .festinalente/glossary.yaml - If both product AND engineering docs updated: git commit -m "docs(#{number}): product+engineering - {summary}" - If only product docs updated: git commit -m "docs(#{number}): product - {summary}" - If only engineering docs updated: git commit -m "docs(#{number}): engineering - {summary}"
After festina-complete marks the task as done, commit: - git add .festinalente/tasks/{id}/task.xml - git commit -m "chore(#{number}): done - {title}"

After updating the plan with the rework report and moving task back to in-progress, commit: - git add .festinalente/tasks/{id}/task.xml - git add .festinalente/tasks/{id}/plan.xml - git commit -m "chore(#{number}): rework - {title}"
After deleting the task folder, stage and commit the deletion: - git add -A .festinalente/tasks/{id}/ - git commit -m "chore(#{number}): delete - {title}"

After implementation and user confirms (pause_for_review), determine commit type from the quick task's label using the commit-type field in workflow.yaml. Default: feat. Stage and commit: - git add {changed code files} - git add .festinalente/quick/{id}/quick.xml - git commit -m "{commitType}(#{number}): {title}"

After quick.xml is updated with completion details (status, files, commit hash, summary), amend the commit to include the updated quick.xml: - git add .festinalente/quick/{id}/quick.xml - git commit --amend --no-edit
If docs were updated, amend the commit to include doc changes: - git add .festinalente/product/ .festinalente/engineering/ .festinalente/quick/{id}/ - git commit --amend --no-edit

After creating/updating product documentation and glossary, stage and commit: - git add .festinalente/product/ .festinalente/glossary.yaml - git commit -m "docs: map-product - {brief summary listing main features}"

After creating/updating engineering documentation and glossary, stage and commit: - git add .festinalente/engineering/ .festinalente/glossary.yaml - git commit -m "docs: map-engineering - {systems, patterns listed}"

After creating the directive file and updating config.yaml, stage and commit: - git add .festinalente/directives/{name}.xml .festinalente/config.yaml - git commit -m "chore: create directive - {name}"

check.item: All file changes were committed with correct message format
Commit messages follow conventional commit format: type(#NNN): description
Scope uses numeric prefix only (e.g., #022), not the full slug
"chore" used for task scaffolding, "docs" reserved for actual documentation
No uncommitted changes remain after skill completion (unless implement phase)

example.code: # Full task lifecycle (task id: 022-add-dark-mode, label: feature): chore(#022): create - Add dark mode toggle # /festina-create chore(#022): scope - Add dark mode toggle # /festina-scope chore(#022): plan - Add dark mode toggle # /festina-plan # /festina-implement (no commit) chore(#022): save - completed toggle and theme provider # /festina-save (optional, repeatable) feat(#022): Add dark mode toggle # /festina-finalize (code + task artifacts) docs(#022): product - dark mode documentation # /festina-finalize (docs, if any) chore(#022): done - Add dark mode toggle # /festina-complete
example.explanation: "chore" for task scaffolding, "docs" only for actual documentation, "feat" for the implementation. Scope is always #NNN.

example.code:
# Commit type determination from task labels: # Task has label "bug" with commit-type "fix" in workflow.yaml # -> fix(#001): Fix login redirect bug
# Task has label "feature" with commit-type "feat" in workflow.yaml # -> feat(#002): Add user authentication
# Task has label "refactor" with commit-type "refactor" in workflow.yaml # -> refactor(#003): Simplify database queries
example.explanation: The commit type comes from the label's commit-type field in workflow.yaml, not from guessing.

example.code:
# WRONG: Using "docs" for task scaffolding docs(#022): create - Add dark mode toggle docs(#022): done - Add dark mode toggle
# CORRECT: "chore" for scaffolding, "docs" for actual documentation chore(#022): create - Add dark mode toggle chore(#022): done - Add dark mode toggle docs(#022): product - dark mode documentation
example.explanation: "docs" is reserved for actual product/engineering documentation updates. Task lifecycle commits use "chore".

example.code: # WRONG: Committing during implement phase git add src/auth.ts git commit -m "feat(#001): partial implementation"
example.explanation: Implementation phase does NOT commit. Use /festina-save for WIP commits, or wait for /festina-finalize.

example.code:
# WRONG: Using invented commit types git commit -m "wip(#001): Add user authentication" git commit -m "quick(#001): Add user authentication"
# CORRECT: Valid types are feat, fix, refactor, docs, chore git commit -m "feat(#001): Add user authentication"
example.explanation: Valid commit types: feat, fix, refactor, docs, chore. No invented types.
